|access-date=2023-03-09 |website=www.etgmr.com}} Amul was formally registered on 14 December 1946 as the Kaira District Co-operative Milk Producers' Union Limited (KDCMPUL).{{cite web |title=The Story of Amul |url=https://www.amuldairy.com/dr_kurien.php |website=Amul Dairy |access-date=2026-05-05}} The cooperative was founded by '''[[Tribhuvandas Kishibhai Patel]]''', who served as its chairman until his retirement in the 1970s. Amul's former Executive Head — [[Verghese Kurien]]; was responsible for spurring [[White revolution (India)|India's White Revolution]], which made the country the world's largest producer of milk/milk products; and it's cooperative model has since been replicated across India, eventually leading it to venture into overseas markets.{{cite news |title=Amul’s global footprint |url=https://www.thehindu.com/business/Industry/amul-to-launch-fresh-milk-in-us-market/article67989917.ece |work=The Hindu |access-date=2026-05-05}}{{Cite web |title=Dairy Articles |url=https://indiadairy.com/dairy-articles/ |access-date=2023-03-09 |website=IndiaDairy |language=en-US |archive-date=9 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230309203116/https://indiadairy.com/dairy-articles/ |url-status=live }}{{cite news|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/amuls-worlds-biggest-vegetarian-cheese-brand/articleshow/1288927.cms|title=Amul's world's biggest vegetarian cheese brand exports cheese to the US, Middle East, Singapore, Hong Kong with sales estimated to touch 600 tonne in 2005|newspaper=The Economic Times|access-date=1 July 2020|last1=Srinivas|first1=Nidhi Nath|archive-date=5 October 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171005134854/http://economictimes.indiatimes.com/amuls-worlds-biggest-vegetarian-cheese-brand/articleshow/1288927.cms|url-status=live}} The White Revolution and the technical success of the union was further supported by '''H. M. Dalaya''', who achieved a global breakthrough by developing the process to produce skim milk powder from buffalo milk—a feat previously deemed impossible by international experts.{{cite web |title=The Birth of Amul |url=https://www.amul.com/m/about-us |website=Amul.com |access-date=2026-05-05}} ==History== [[File:2_The-Amul-trinity_Kurien_Shri-TK-Patel_HM_Dalaya.jpg|thumbnail|250px |[[Verghese Kurien]], [[Tribhuvandas Kishibhai Patel]], and [[Harichand Megha Dalaya]]]] === Early years (1946-1970) === Amul was founded on 14 December 1946 as a response to the exploitation of small dairy farmers by traders and agents. At the time, milk prices were arbitrarily determined, giving [[Polson (brand)|Polson]] an effective monopoly in milk collection from Kaira and its subsequent supply to [[Mumbai]].{{Cite book |last=George |first=Shanti |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=dbI6AAAAMAAJ |title=Operation Flood: An Appraisal of Current Indian Dairy Policy |date=1985 |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=978-0-19-561679-8 |language=en |access-date=9 March 2023 |archive-date=4 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230404052239/https://books.google.com/books?id=dbI6AAAAMAAJ |url-status=live }}{{cite book |last=Heredia |first=Ruth |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=TYEkjpYkHrMC |title=The Amul India story |publisher=Tata McGraw-Hill |year=1997 |location=New Delhi|isbn=9780074631607 }}{{Cite news|title= Story of Cooperation|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q9DTUn4Bz4E|date=20 September 2025}} Frustrated with the trade practices (which they perceived as unfair), the farmers of Kaira, led by [[Tribhuvandas Kishibhai Patel]], approached [[Vallabhbhai Patel]], who advised them to form a cooperative. If they did so, they would be able to directly supply their milk to the Bombay Milk Scheme instead of working for Polson.{{cite news|last=Suhrud|first=Tridip|author-link=Tridip Suhrud|title=The magic of manthan|url=http://www.tehelka.com/story_main17.asp?filename=op040806the_magic.asp|access-date=2 February 2011|newspaper=Tehelka|date=8 April 2006|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061111211535/http://www.tehelka.com/story_main17.asp?filename=op040806the_magic.asp|archive-date=11 November 2006|url-status=dead}} Sardar Patel sent [[Morarji Desai]] to organise the farmers. Following a meeting in [[Chaklasi]], the farmers formed the cooperative and resolved not to provide Polson with any more milk. Milk collection was decentralised, as most producers were marginal farmers who could deliver, at most, 1–2 litres of milk per day. Cooperatives were formed for each village.{{cite journal |last=Thapar |first=Romila |title=Seminar, Issues 497–508 |journal=Seminar|year=2001}} The cooperative was strict that any farmer could become a member, irrespective of their religion, caste, gender, or political affiliation.{{cite book |last1=Kurien |first1=Verghese |last2=Salvi |first2=Gouri |title=I Too Had a Dream |publisher=Roli Books |year=2005 |isbn=978-81-7436-407-4 |page=179 }} By June 1948, the KDCMPUL had started pasteurising milk for the Bombay Milk Scheme. Then-Prime Minister [[Lal Bahadur Shastri]] visited [[Anand, Gujarat|Anand]] to inaugurate Amul's cattle feed factory. One year later, in 1949, Tribhuvandas Patel hired '''[[Verghese Kurien]]''', initially as a dairy engineer to assist with machinery.{{cite book |last1=Kurien |first1=Verghese |last2=Salve |first2=Gerson |title=I Too Had a Dream |date=2005 |publisher=APH Publishing |isbn=978-8174364074}} Kurien eventually became the General Manager, where he provided the strategic vision and professional management that scaled the "Anand Pattern" of cooperatives. He is recognized as the '''"Father of the White Revolution"''' for spearheading [[Operation Flood]], which transformed India from a milk-deficient nation into the world's largest producer of milk.{{cite web |title=About the Milkman of India |url=https://www.nddb.coop/about/genesis/kurien |website=National Dairy Development Board |access-date=2026-05-05}} Kurien is credited with the revolutionary marketing and branding efforts of Amul, ensuring that the primary producer received the largest share of the consumer's rupee. On 31 October 1964, Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri spoke to farmers about their cooperative. After returning to Delhi, he set in motion the creation of an organisation, the [[National Dairy Development Board]] (NDDB), to replicate the Kaira cooperative in other parts of India. === The White Revolution (1970 onwards) === The cooperative was further developed through the efforts of Verghese Kurien and [[Harichand Megha Dalaya|H. M. Dalaya]]. Dalaya's innovation of making [[Skimmed milk|skim milk]] powder from buffalo milk was a technological breakthrough that revolutionised India's organised dairy industry.{{cite book |last=Kurien |first=Verghese |title=Ending Poverty in South Asia: Ideas that work |year=2007 |publisher=The World Bank |location=Washington D.C., USA |isbn=978-0-8213-6876-3 |chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=IV9m8gF6XDcC&pg=PA47 |chapter=India' s Milk Revolution: Investing in Rural Producer Organizations |editor=Narayan, Deepa |editor2=Glinskaya, Elena |access-date=13 January 2021 |page=47 |quote=If there was one technological breakthrough that revolutionized India's organized dairy industry, it was the making of skim milk powder out of buffalo milk. The man who made this possible and who had the foresight to defy the prevailing technical wisdom was H. M. Dalaya. |archive-date=9 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230309030609/https://books.google.com/books?id=IV9m8gF6XDcC&pg=PA47 |url-status=live }} With Kurien's help, the process was expanded on a commercial scale, which led to the first modern dairy cooperative at Anand. This cooperative would go on to compete against the established players in the market.{{cite journal|title=Economic and political weekly, Volume 6, Part 4|journal=Economic and Political Weekly|year=1971|volume=6}} The success of the trio (T. K. Patel, Kurien, and Dalaya) at the cooperative's dairy soon spread to Anand's neighbourhood in Gujarat. Within a short span, five unions in other districts—[[Mehsana]], [[Banaskantha district|Banaskantha]], [[Vadodara|Baroda]], [[Sabarkantha district|Sabarkantha]], and [[Surat]]—were set up, following the approach sometimes described as ''the Anand pattern''. In 1970, the cooperative spearheaded the "[[White revolution (India)|White Revolution]]" of India. To combine forces and expand the market while saving on advertising and avoiding competing against each other, the Gujarat Co-operative Milk Marketing Federation Ltd., an apex marketing body of these district cooperatives, was set up in 1973. The Kaira Union, which had the brand name Amul with it since 1955, transferred it to GCMMF. Technological developments at Amul have subsequently spread to other parts of India.{{cite book|title=The Cheese Industry in India|publisher=Chillibreeze}} Under the leadership of Tribhuvandas Patel, in 1973, Amul celebrated its 25th anniversary with Morarji Desai, [[Maniben Patel]], and [[Verghese Kurien]].{{cite news |last1=Gupta |first1=Sharad |title=Remembering Verghese Kurien – India's first milkman |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/news/variety/remembering-verghese-kurien-indias-first-milkman/article30084051.ece |access-date=10 March 2021 |publisher=businessline |language=en |archive-date=21 October 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211021222527/https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/news/variety/remembering-verghese-kurien-indias-first-milkman/article30084051.ece |url-status=live }} In 1999, it was awarded the "Best of All" [[Rajiv Gandhi National Quality Award]].{{cite web | url = http://www.bis.org.in/other/rgnqa_win_12.pdf | title = Annex iv: list of award winners of Rajiv Gandhi national quality awards | last1 = Shrawan | date = 29 May 2013 | website = bis.org.in | publisher = Bureau of Indian Standards | location = New Delhi | access-date = 15 May 2014 | archive-date = 2 December 2014 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20141202153812/http://www.bis.org.in/other/rgnqa_win_12.pdf | url-status = live }} In 2025, Amul was ranked third most valued brand in India in the YouGov India Value Rankings 2025.{{Cite web |date=2025-03-06 |title=Amul ranked among India's most valued brands, the only FMCG in the top 3 list |url=https://www.financialexpress.com/business/industry-amul-ranked-among-indias-most-valued-brands-the-only-fmcg-in-the-top-3-list-3769863/ |access-date=2025-03-11 |website=Financialexpress |language=en}} ==Organisation: Three tiers of hierarchical co-operative societies== {{anchor| Org | Organisation | Organization | Tier | Tiers | Hierarchy | Hierarchical }} Amul operates on a [[Cooperative movement in India|three-tier co-operative society model]] of dairy development is a structure, where milk producers form the village level dairy cooperative societies, federated under a milk union at the district level which are further federation as member unions at the state level. Amul at village and district level is managed by the elected officials. The three-tiered structure, known as the '''"Anand Pattern of co-operative societies"''', has the following hierarchical levels:[https://amul.com/m/about-us About AMul], Amul, accessed 19 Sept 2025. # '''Village level society''' - '''Village Dairy Cooperative Society''' ('''VDCS'''): Milk producers in a village come together to form this primary society, which collects surplus milk and provides support services to its members. Members elect the management council, i.e. village level societies are self-managed by the elected members. # '''District level union of societies''' - '''District Cooperative Milk Producers Union''' ('''DCMPU''') or '''Dugdh Sangh''': Village-level societies within a district become members of a district milk union, which is responsible for procuring, processing, and transporting milk. Each village level council with one vote each is member of district level union and they elect the district level council, i.e. district level unions are self-managed by the elected members. [[Banas Dairy]] of [[ Banaskantha district]] and [[Dudhsagar Dairy]] of [[Mehsana district]] in Gujarat are examples of district level union of societies. # '''State level federation of state level unions''' - '''State Cooperative Milk Federation''' ('''SCMF'''): The district milk unions within a state are federated under a state-level organization. This federation is in charge of marketing and distributing milk and milk products. In the case of Amul, the state federation is the Gujarat Cooperative Milk Marketing Federation Ltd. (GCMMF). Each district level union with one vote each is a member of state level union and they elect the state level council. The elected state level federation's elected council hires the corporate-style outsider professionals managers to run the operation to give it the professional competitive edge. * Not part of Amul structure: There are other co-operative societies in India with 4 layers which also have 4th level at national level, such as '''National Cooperative Dairy Federation of India''' ('''NCDFI''') **4. '''National level federation of state level federations''': While Amul has 3-tier statewide structure across Gujarat state only, there are other national-level cooperative dairy organizations in India. The National Cooperative Dairy Federation of India (NCDFI) is the apex body for the country's cooperative dairy sector and is based in Anand city in Gujarat. Amul and various state-level milk co-operative of respective states are members of NCDFI, such as [[Haryana Dairy Development Cooperative Federation Ltd]] (sells products under ''"Vita"'' brand), [[Kerala Co-operative Milk Marketing Federation]], [[Karnataka Milk Federation]], [[Mother Dairy]] in Delhi, etc. All these were developed with the help of [[National Dairy Development Board]]. Similarly, there are [[#Coop|several other hierarchical co-operative societies in India]] focused on various other products, such as [[Coffee Board of India|coffee]], [[Coconut Development Board|Cocconut]], [[Coir Board of India|coir]], [[Spices Board of India|spices]], [[Tea Board of India|tea]], and many more. ==Processing== Amul has several plants for processing dairy products. In 2025, Amul's Sabar Dairy Plant at [[Haryana_State_Industrial_and_Infrastructure_Development_Corporation#Industrial_estates_and_townships|IMT Rohtak]] in [[Haryana]] state was expanded making it India's largest processing plant for curd, buttermilk, and yoghurt catering for the Haryana, Delhi-NCR, and northern India region. In 2025, every day it processes 150 mt (metric ton) curd, 10 mt yoghurt, 10 mt sweets, and 3 mt of buttermilk. In 2025, [[Central_Institute_for_Research_on_Buffaloes#Milk_products|Haryana was India's third largest producer of milk]] (122.2 lakh tonnes per year) with highest per capita milk availability in India (1,105 grams per day).[https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/chandigarh/sabar-dairy-expansion-a-milestone-for-haryana-amit-shah-10285640/ Sabar Dairy expansion a milestone for Haryana: Amit Shah], Indian Express, 3 Oct 2025. ==Partnerships== Amul has entered into partnerships with cooperative organisations internationally. In May 2024, it signed an agreement to market Amul-branded fresh milk in the United States in collaboration with the Michigan Milk Producers Association, using locally produced milk and Amul formulations.{{cite news |last=Langa |first=Mahesh |title=Amul goes to U.S., partners Michigan milk producers’ body to sell fresh milk |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/other-states/amul-goes-to-us-partners-michigan-milk-producers-body-to-sell-fresh-milk/article68197242.ece |work=The Hindu |date=20 May 2024 |access-date=28 February 2026}} In June 2025, the cooperative launched Amul milk in Spain through a partnership with a Spanish dairy cooperative.{{cite news |title=GCMMF launches Amul Milk in Spain |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/cons-products/food/gcmmf-launches-amul-milk-in-spain/articleshow/121626489.cms |work=The Economic Times |date=4 June 2025 |access-date=28 February 2026}} ==Marketing== {{See also|Amul girl}} In 1966, Amul hired Sylvester daCunha, the managing director of an advertising agency, to design an ad campaign for Amul Butter. DaCunha created an operation consisting of a series of hoardings featuring topical ads related to day-to-day issues.{{cite web|last=Varma|first=Mini|title=The moppet who put Amul on India's breakfast table|url=http://www.amul.com/story.html|publisher=Amul|access-date=2 February 2011|archive-date=13 June 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110613085925/http://www.amul.com/story.html|url-status=live}} It was popular and earned a Guinness World Record for the longest-running ad campaign in the world. In the 1980s, cartoon artist Kumar Morey and scriptwriter Bharat Dabholkar were involved in sketching the Amul ads; the latter rejected the trend of using celebrities in advertisement campaigns. Dabholkar credited chairman Verghese Kurien with creating a free atmosphere that fostered the development of the ads.{{cite news|last=Rao|first=Subha J.|title=Punch guru|url=http://www.hindu.com/thehindu/mp/2007/12/15/stories/2007121551330100.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121108194414/http://www.hindu.com/thehindu/mp/2007/12/15/stories/2007121551330100.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=8 November 2012|access-date=2 February 2011|date=15 December 2007|newspaper=[[The Hindu]]|location=Chennai, India}} Despite encountering political pressure on several occasions, daCunha's agency has made it a policy not to back down. Some of the more controversial Amul ads include one commenting on the Naxalite uprising in West Bengal, one on the Indian Airlines employees' strike, and one depicting the Amul girl wearing a Gandhi cap. In 2013, Amul tweeted a picture featuring the [[Amul girl|Amul Butter Girl]], implying that "freedom of choice" died in 2013, in opposition to the [[Supreme Court of India]] overruling the judgment of the [[Delhi High Court|High Court of Delhi]] and criminalising [[homosexuality]] again.{{cite news | url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/Brands-peek-out-of-the-closet/articleshow/27248253.cms | work=The Times of India | title=Brands peek out of the closet – The Times of India | access-date=28 March 2014 | archive-date=13 December 2013 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131213015210/http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/Brands-peek-out-of-the-closet/articleshow/27248253.cms | url-status=live }} On 17 October 2016, the Amul Butter Girl celebrated 50 years since she first appeared in the topical ad, titled "Thoroughbred". The ad showed a jockey holding a slice of bread during the horse race season in 1966. The impish Amul girl had appeared for the first time even before that, with Eustace Fernandez showing her offering bedtime prayers with a wink and a lick of lips, saying "Give us this day our daily bread: with Amul butter".{{cite web |date=16 October 2016 |title=In pics Fifty years on, Amul's 'utterly butterly' girl is still a delight |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/in-pics-fifty-years-on-amul-s-utterly-butterly-girl-is-still-a-delight/story-jY5tN55PJQh6b5Ftcbzb5J.html |website=Hindustan Times |publisher= |access-date=23 January 2023 |archive-date=23 January 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230123145835/https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/in-pics-fifty-years-on-amul-s-utterly-butterly-girl-is-still-a-delight/story-jY5tN55PJQh6b5Ftcbzb5J.html |url-status=live }} Their ad on ''Aagey Badhta Hai India'' had an excellent response from the audience. It spoke about how their milk is seen as a household product, with a catchy tune associated with it. It has over 39 lakh (3.9 million) views on YouTube.Archived at [https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211211/zIQTwukIDyg Ghostarchive]{{cbignore}} and the [https://web.archive.org/web/20200708195023/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zIQTwukIDyg Wayback Machine]{{cbignore}}: {{Citation|last=Amul The Taste of India|title=Amul Milk – Aage Badta Hai India|date=10 July 2015|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zIQTwukIDyg|access-date=9 April 2019}}{{cbignore}} In February 2020, Amul posted a picture of the Amul girl treating [[Joaquin Phoenix]] with butter after his academy award win for his role in the 2019 film, [[Joker (2019 film)|''Joker'']].{{cite web |date=12 February 2020 |title=Amul smears butter on vegan Joaquin Phoenix's face in an ad celebrating Oscar win, gets slammed by PETA |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/hollywood/amul-smears-butter-on-vegan-joaquin-phoenix-s-face-in-ad-celebrating-oscar-win-gets-slammed-by-peta/story-Fx77XbHBFcolop5LYcY7mM.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200212132923/https://www.hindustantimes.com/hollywood/amul-smears-butter-on-vegan-joaquin-phoenix-s-face-in-ad-celebrating-oscar-win-gets-slammed-by-peta/story-Fx77XbHBFcolop5LYcY7mM.html |archive-date=12 February 2020 |access-date=3 May 2021 |website=[[Hindustan Times]] |publisher=Indo Asian News Service |language=en}} Since Phoenix is a vegan, Amul faced criticism from vegans in India and PETA for the poor knowledge of his vegan activism and life. In July 2024, Amul featured [[Maya Neelakantan]], a ten-year-old guitar prodigy who auditioned for [[America's Got Talent season 19|''America's Got Talent'' season 19]] in June 2024.{{Cite web |last=Baruah |first=Akashdeep |date=2024-07-08 |title=Amul pays tribute to 'Rock Goddess' Maya Neelakantan - CNBC TV18 |url=https://www.cnbctv18.com/entertainment/amul-tribute-rock-goddess-maya-neelakantan-americas-got-talent-papa-roach-last-resort-19439882.htm |access-date=2024-07-23 |website=CNBCTV18 |language=en}} ==In popular culture== The White Revolution inspired filmmaker [[Shyam Benegal]] to base his 1976 film ''[[Manthan]]'' on it. The film was financed by over five lakh (half a million) rural farmers in Gujarat, who contributed ₹2 each to its budget. Upon its release, these farmers went in truckloads to watch 'their' film, making it a commercial success.{{Cite web |date=2007-08-08 |title=Phalke award for Benegal |url=http://www.ndtvmovies.com/newstory.asp?section=Movies&id=ENTEN20070021927 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110719065444/http://www.ndtvmovies.com/movie_Story.aspx?id=ENTEN20070021927&keyword=&subcatg= |archive-date=2011-07-19 |access-date=2023-03-09 |website=[[NDTV]]}}{{Cite web |title=Manas: Culture, Indian Cinema- Shyam Benegal |url=http://www.sscnet.ucla.edu/southasia/Culture/Cinema/Benegal.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120805163057/http://www.sscnet.ucla.edu/southasia/Culture/Cinema/Benegal.html |archive-date=2012-08-05 |access-date=2023-03-09 |website=www.sscnet.ucla.edu}} The Anand Milk Union Limited, commonly known as Amul, is an Indian dairy brand owned by the cooperative society, Gujarat Cooperative Milk Marketing Federation (GCMMF), based in Anand, Gujarat. GCMMF is controlled by 3.6 million milk producers.
Amul was formally registered on 14 December 1946 as the Kaira District Co-operative Milk Producers' Union Limited (KDCMPUL). The cooperative was founded by Tribhuvandas Kishibhai Patel, who served as its chairman until his retirement in the 1970s.
Amul's former Executive Head — Verghese Kurien; was responsible for spurring India's White Revolution, which made the country the world's largest producer of milk/milk products; and it's cooperative model has since been replicated across India, eventually leading it to venture into overseas markets.
The White Revolution and the technical success of the union was further supported by H. M. Dalaya, who achieved a global breakthrough by developing the process to produce skim milk powder from buffalo milk—a feat previously deemed impossible by international experts.
